Web Server Manager (Linux ADOM)

A cPanel-style manager for Linux web servers, in the Linux ADOM. You sign in with your own SSH account; when it is not allowed to do something, SATOM uses sudo exactly as you set it on your credential. Server health (memory, disks, load, processes, failed services) through the agent or plain SSH as you choose, maintenance that drains the server from its FortiWeb/FortiADC pools first, files, websites, certificates, security, .htaccess, scripts, cron, packages, services, logs, users and SSH — on Debian, SUSE and RHEL-family servers, with every operation audited.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionswebserver.view webserver.files webserver.sites webserver.system webserver.root webserver.credentials
📍 WhereLinux ADOM → Web Server Manager (/webserver/); the plugins for automation in Plugin Studio

What is it?#

Web Server Manager administers Linux web servers from the Linux ADOM, the way a hosting panel does — without installing anything on the server and with your own SSH account. The Web hosts example apps of Plugin Studio stay next to it in the Linux ADOM's Plugins: they handle a server's virtual hosts, files and certificates through the restricted satom-webctl agent, and their server connection is also a server of the manager.

It is a basic element of the Linux ADOM: Linux → Web Server Manager in the menu. An administrator switches it on or off per ADOM (Settings → ADOMs → Web Server Manager). The same operations are also thirteen signed plugins (bundle web-server-manager) for automations and other apps.

❗Important

Every operation runs as the SSH account of the credential you pick. SATOM uses sudo only when the credential allows it and your SATOM profile has Run as root. It never edits the server's sudo rules and never stores a root password. A managed server can never open a connection to SATOM (hostguard).

How to use#

  1. Linux → Web Server Manager → Add server: name, host, SSH port.
  2. On the server's Overview, press Fetch and trust (the host key). Nothing is sent to an untrusted server, and a changed key is refused.
  3. Add credential: your SSH user and password, or a private key (paste one, or let SATOM generate the pair and add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys).
  4. Choose how SATOM becomes root: never, sudo with a password (your SSH password, or asked every time), sudo -i -u root with a password (the server only lets your account open root's login shell — e.g. sign in as ebc, then sudo -i -u root with the password of ebc; same password choices) or sudo without password (the server has a NOPASSWD rule).
  5. Choose Run as: Automatic (your account; when the server says permission denied, the same operation again through sudo), always my account or always root.
  6. Press Check access: SATOM tells you who you are on the server and whether sudo works.

Untick SATOM keeps the secret to be asked for the password at every operation; it is used for that call and forgotten.

Installing the plugins#

  1. Plugin Studio → Import package or bundle: pick web-server-manager-<version>.satombundle (staging hub, downloads/plugins/).
  2. Folder: Web Server Manager. Import.
  3. Plugin Studio → Folders → Web Server Manager: tick the Linux ADOM (and a user group, if you want to hand the apps to one).
  4. Publish each app.

Every app's form asks for the server, optionally a credential (empty = your own for that server, otherwise a shared one), the run-as and two password fields, SSH password and sudo password, which you fill only when the credential does not keep its secret or sudo asks. They are used for that call and never kept in the run.

ℹ️Note

An app never widens who may do what: it answers for the person who runs it, with the same checks as the pages. A rehearsal runs the reading steps and only describes the changing ones.

Who reaches which server and site?#

In Access → Profiles → Devices, under the Linux ADOM, tick servers (none = all) and, under a server, sites (none = the whole server).

  • Some servers: the others are not listed and their pages answer not found.
  • Some sites: the profile opens File Manager, Domains & VHosts and .htaccess of that server for those sites only. Its files are confined to the sites' document roots by the helper on the server (symlinks resolved). Packages, services, users, SSH, cron, security, certificates, scripts and logs act on the whole server and are refused.

The sites offered are the ones the server last listed: open its Domains & VHosts page to refresh them.

What can I do?#

Module Highlights
Health Memory, swap, disks (space and inodes), CPU and load, top processes, failed services; history charts; thresholds and bell per server
Maintenance Out of the FortiWeb / FortiADC pools, restart a service or run a script, check, back in — every device write re-read
File Manager Opens in your home folder (a site's Files button opens the site's folder; the globe button, the web sites folder: /srv/www/vhosts on SUSE); As: the credential's setting, your account or root, and Open as root when your account cannot read a folder. Any folder your account may read; editor with syntax highlighting; upload, download, preview; chmod/chown; zip, tar.gz, extract (unsafe archives refused); search; History and restore of every file SATOM overwrote
Domains & VHosts nginx or Apache; static, PHP-FPM or reverse proxy; HTTP and HTTPS ports of your choice (Apache gets the Listen line); document root filled in from the domain; a new folder owned by the web server's account (wwwrun:www on SUSE Apache, www-data on Debian, apache/nginx on RHEL); HTTPS and redirect, limits, headers, own logs; tested before reload, restored if the test fails
SSL Certificates Internal CA (key made on the server), import, certbot (Let's Encrypt), renew, auto-renewal, TLS check, expiry warnings
Security Score, findings with Fix buttons, firewall, fail2ban, failed logins, open ports
.htaccess Wizard and templates (WordPress, Joomla, Laravel…). On nginx the rules are converted; what cannot be converted is listed and not applied
Scripts Library, upload, run with a preview of user, folder, command and parameters; output, errors and exit code kept
Cron Jobs Your crontab (or another account's, as root) with a frequency builder, and jobs SATOM runs with a service credential. A save goes to the crontab that was loaded, also when auto retries through sudo
Package Manager apt, dnf, zypper: search, updates, and a plan of what changes before every install or removal
Services, Logs systemd services, opening on the running ones (views: Running, Web-server services, Failed, All); web, PHP, system, auth and cron logs; the journal, live
Users, SSH Accounts and groups; sshd settings tested with sshd -t; authorized keys

Server health: agent or plain SSH?#

Linux → Web Server Manager → server → Health shows the whole machine and keeps it in the metrics store (charts for 6 h, 24 h, 7 days). How SATOM reads it is your choice, in Health → Settings:

Choice On the server
Automatic The agent when the server has a working one (installed and checked by SATOM, or installed by hand), otherwise a shared SSH credential. When the server refuses the agent's key, the reading is made with that credential and the page says why the agent was not used.
The satom-webctl agent Installed with Install the satom-webctl agent (Overview or Health › Settings: SATOM runs its installer as root with the selected credential and its own key, valid only from the SATOM nodes) or by hand with install-satom-webctl.sh: account satom-mon, SATOM's own key, a forced command, no shell, nobody's password. Needs satom-webctl 1.2.0 or newer.
SSH with a credential I pick Nothing installed. A credential marked Shared that keeps its secret signs in and the helper travels on the session.
Off Not read.

The reading never uses sudo and never writes. Thresholds per server (disk, inodes, free memory, swap, load per CPU — not judged in a container, where the load is the host's — and failed services, with patterns to ignore). The bell rings once per new or worse problem and once on recovery; a server that cannot be read is unreachable after two failed readings in a row.

The agent: install, reinstall, remove#

On the server's Overview › Agent (also in Health › Settings, and in Health's warning when the server refuses the agent's key) pick a credential that can become root in Sign in as, then:

Button What it does
Install agent Runs install-satom-webctl.sh as root with SATOM's own key, valid only from the SATOM nodes, then checks that satom-mon signs in with that key. An install that does not pass the check is reported as failed.
Reinstall agent Removes it exactly as the installer added it, checks that the server now refuses the key, installs it again with the same key and checks the sign-in. A second reinstall changes nothing (0 changes). Use it after a failed install, when the key changed, or to update the agent.
Remove agent Removes the program, its configuration, the two sudo rules per web server, the ACLs and SATOM's key line, and the account satom-mon only if the installer created it; checks that the server refuses the key; then SATOM forgets the key and the satom-webctl agent credential. Also delete backups, log and certificates adds --purge (certificates a site still uses are kept).

Each one asks for confirmation and runs as a job: its steps appear under the buttons and in the Job Manager, and one line sums it up in the audit log (wsm.agent.<action>_job). No secret reaches a step or a log. The badge says what SATOM knows: Installed, Installed (not checked by SATOM) (installed by hand), Install not confirmed, Install failed, Key changed: reinstall, Removed or Not installed. Needs Administer servers, Run as root and Allow changes on the server, and a credential that may be used for health: a credential limited to some modules needs health ticked (Overview › Credentials › Edit), and without it the button is refused before any job starts.

Maintenance: out of the pool, work, back in#

  1. Maintenance → Find pool members: SATOM asks every FortiWeb and FortiADC you reach for the members whose address is this server's. Tick the ones that are this server and Keep.
  2. Run a maintenance: restart or reload a service, run a library script, or Only drain while you work. SATOM checks it would not empty a pool, keeps each member's status, drains it (maintain or disable, re-read from the device), waits, does the work, checks the server (health, the service, the site on the member's port) and puts each member back to the status it had before, re-read.
  3. If the work or the check fails the members stay drained (default), the administrators get a bell, and the page offers Return to service.

Changing a pool member needs Apply network. Dry run shows the changes and makes none.

What happens when a credential is revoked?#

Its stored secret is erased immediately. Every job SATOM had scheduled with it stops and shows waiting for authentication, and the administrators get a bell notification. The jobs are kept: pick another credential and they run again.

Where is everything logged?#

/webserver/audit (Operations log): time, your SATOM user, the SSH user, the Linux user that actually ran the operation, whether sudo was used, the credential, the result and the session id. Export it as CSV.

Troubleshooting#

You see Why, and what to do
has no trusted host key yet Press Fetch and trust on the server's Overview.
the host key changed The server was rebuilt, or something answers in its place. Check the fingerprint on the server, then trust the new key.
refused the sign-in Wrong user, password or key, or the server does not accept that method (it lists the ones it accepts).
sudo did not accept the password The sudo password is wrong; with asked every time you are asked again.
sudo asks for a password … NOPASSWD The credential says NOPASSWD but the server has no such rule: change the credential to sudo with a password.
not allowed to use sudo with sudo -i -u root The server's rules do not let the account open root's shell; try sudo with a password, or ask the server's administrator.
not allowed to use sudo The account is not in the server's sudo rules (sudo/wheel group). Ask the server's administrator.
needs administrator rights Your credential does not use sudo, or your SATOM profile lacks Run as root.
read-only in SATOM Turn on Allow changes on the server's Overview.
credential … is not allowed for Health (it is limited to …) The credential may only be used for the modules ticked on it. Edit it on the server's Overview › Credentials and tick health (it covers Install / Reinstall / Remove agent), or pick another credential in Sign in as. Before 4.11.14 health could not be ticked and the job failed after signing in.
you have no credential for … (an app) Add your SSH account on the server's page, or ask an administrator to share one.
credential … needs Password for this call (an app) The credential does not keep its secret: fill SSH password (and sudo password if sudo asks) in the app's form.
An app is missing from Plugins The folder Web Server Manager needs the Linux ADOM (Folders), and the app must be switched on and published.
Web Server Manager is not in the menu, its pages say not found The module is switched off: Settings → ADOMs → the Linux row → Web Server Manager.
outside the sites your SATOM profile reaches The profile reaches only some sites: the path (or the target of a link in it) is outside their document roots.
your profile reaches only some sites of … That module acts on the whole server; the profile reaches only some sites of it.
python3 is not installed Install python3 on the server: the manager runs its helper with it.
Health: the satom-webctl agent on the server is older than 1.2.0 Run the installer of this SATOM again on the server, or read it over SSH (Health → Settings).
Health: no way to read it unattended Install the agent, or mark one credential Shared with Keep the secret.
Health: refused SATOM's key for satom-mon The server did not accept the agent key: the agent was never installed with this SATOM's key, its install failed, it was removed, the key changed, or sshd keeps satom-mon out (AllowUsers, AllowGroups, DenyUsers, or the SATOM addresses the key is valid from). Press Reinstall agent in the yellow box; the installer's output in the job names an sshd rule that blocks it. An agent installed before 4.11.12 from a node registered as 127.0.0.1 in the HA list needs one reinstall.
Health: load shown but not judged The server is a container: its load average is the host's.
Maintenance: the last member in service of its pool Draining it stops the service: tick Allow the last member only if that is what you want.
Maintenance: Invalid VM License when finding members That FortiWeb/FortiADC refuses every REST call until it is licensed; the others are still read.
Maintenance: errcode -651 on a FortiWeb member The status maintenance is refused by FortiWeb's REST API; SATOM sends maintain (the GUI's Maintenance).
Scheduled job waiting for authentication Its credential was revoked, disabled, expired, or asks for its secret: pick a service credential that keeps its secret.

Which servers?#

The distributions SATOM itself is deployed on: Debian 12, SUSE Linux Enterprise / openSUSE 15, RHEL 9 / Rocky / AlmaLinux. The server needs SSH and python3 (3.6 or newer, present on all of them).
